question: In 2019, which of the following nations won the FIFA Women’s World Cup?
solution:
The correct answer is __**United States of America**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• USA won FIFA Women’s World Cup 2019.
 
• The eighth edition of the FIFA Women's World Cup was hosted in France.

 
• 24 countries were participated to win the coveted cup and a cash prize of four million USD.
 
• FIFA Women’s World Cup 2019
 
 
• ​Champion: United States (4th title)
 
• Player of the Match: Megan Rapinoe
 
• Runner-up: Netherland
 
• Third place: Sweden
 
 
 
• ​The 2023 FIFA Women's World Cup is scheduled to be the 9th edition of the FIFA Women's World Cup
 
• The tournament will be jointly hosted by Australia and New Zealand and is scheduled to take place from 20 July to 20 August 2023.​​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• The FIFA Women's World Cup was founded in 1991.

 
 
• The first WWC tournament was held 61 years after the men's first FIFA World Cup in 1930.
 
• China was the first country to host the WWC tournament.
 
• Since then, it has been held in Sweden, Germany, Canada, twice in China and the US, and is now being held in France.
 
• Australian Ellyse Perry has appeared in both the women's cricket (2009) and football World Cup (2011).
 
• The 2015 FIFA World Cup featured the youngest coach in World Cup history - Ecuador's Vanessa Arauz, at 26 years.
 
• In 2015, 750 million people tuned in to watch the FIFA women's world cup, held in Canada.
